description: Main track presentations from DEF CON 25, covering offensive and defensive security research, infrastructure security, and emerging attack techniques across multiple domains.

talks.title: The spear to break the security wall of S7CommPlus
talks.teaser: Breaking the encryption in Siemens S7CommPlus protocol to control PLC devices despite security reinforcements.
talks.summary:
Industrial Control System Security

Attacks against industrial control systems have increased year over year. The Stuxnet attack in 2010 exploited the insecurity of the S7Comm protocol, prompting Siemens to implement security reinforcements in the S7CommPlus protocol, which includes encryption.

Analyzing the Protocol

The talk uses Wireshark to analyze communications between Siemens TIA Portal and PLC devices. Through reverse debugging with WinDbg and IDA, researchers demonstrate how to break the encryption in the S7CommPlus protocol. The analysis reveals vulnerabilities despite encryption implementation.

Demonstration and Control

The researchers created an MFC program capable of controlling the start and stop of PLCs and modifying digital and analog inputs and outputs. This demonstrates complete control over protected industrial systems.

Security Recommendations

Based on this research, the presentation proposes security improvements at both the code level and protocol level to enhance the protection of Siemens PLC devices against similar attacks.

talks.title: Breaking the x86 Instruction Set
talks.teaser: Exhaustively searching the x86 instruction set to uncover secret instructions, hardware glitches, and hypervisor flaws.
talks.summary:
Hardware Reverse Engineering

Modern x86 processors contain secret instructions and hardware bugs beyond documented specifications. The presentation demonstrates how page fault analysis and creative processor fuzzing exhaustively search the x86 instruction set to discover undocumented functionality.

Research Methodology

Using fuzzing techniques against the processor itself, researchers identify execution patterns that reveal hidden instructions and hardware behaviors. This approach uncovers secrets buried in chipsets and processor implementations.

Findings and Impact

The research discloses new x86 hardware glitches, previously unknown machine instructions, and ubiquitous software bugs. Additionally, the work reveals flaws in enterprise hypervisors that make use of x86 features.

Tooling Release

The Sandsifter toolset is released to allow security researchers to audit and break their own processors, democratizing the ability to discover processor vulnerabilities and undocumented behaviors.

talks.title: Weaponizing the BBC Micro Bit
talks.teaser: Transforming an educational device into a portable wireless attack tool for RF protocol exploitation.
talks.summary:
Educational Device Security

The BBC Micro:Bit was launched in 2015 as an affordable coding device for students in the UK. The device uses a 2.4GHz RF chip from Nordic Semiconductor, making it potentially exploitable for wireless attacks.

Firmware Exploitation

Researchers discovered how to hack into the Micro:Bit firmware and transform it into a powerful attack tool. The device becomes capable of sniffing keystrokes from wireless keyboards and hijacking quadcopters during flight, achieving complete control.

Tools and Protocols

The team developed tools for security researchers to interact with proprietary 2.4GHz protocols. They created an improved sniffer tool inspired by Bastille's mousejack research, enabling comprehensive wireless protocol analysis.

Open Source Release

The source code for the custom firmware and related tools was released at the conference, making the Micro:Bit a accessible platform for creating portable RF attack tools and simplifying security research on 2.4GHz protocols.

talks.title: Real time RFID Cloning in the Field
talks.teaser: Dramatically faster method for cloning RFID credentials in the field that transforms red team engagements.
talks.summary:
RFID Cloning Techniques

Traditional RFID cloning methods in the field work fine but are slow, tedious, and error-prone. The presentation introduces a smarter approach to cloning RFID credentials that is vastly more efficient and practical.

Current Tools and Methods

The talk reviews existing tools and methodologies for long-range RFID cloning. These established approaches establish the baseline for what is possible with conventional techniques.

New Methodology

A novel method is demonstrated that allows cloning RFID credentials in the field in just seconds. This dramatically improves the practical efficiency of credential cloning during penetration testing engagements.

Practical Impact

The new approach changes the way red teams perform physical security assessments, making RFID credential cloning a fast and reliable component of field operations rather than a tedious bottleneck.

talks.title: Revoke Obfuscation: PowerShell Obfuscation
talks.teaser: Framework using statistical analysis to detect and defeat PowerShell obfuscation and evasion techniques.
talks.summary:
PowerShell in Attacks

Attackers, administrators, and legitimate products rely on PowerShell. Its power has made it attractive for attackers and commodity malware. The challenge is separating legitimate use from malicious activity.

Detection Challenges

A/V signatures applied to command line arguments work sometimes. AMSI-based detection performs better. However, obfuscation and evasion techniques like Invoke-Obfuscation can bypass both approaches.

Revoke-Obfuscation Framework

The framework transforms evasion into detection through unique statistical analysis techniques. It examines PowerShell scripts and structures to turn obfuscation into a spotlight. The framework works with .evtx files, command lines, scripts, ScriptBlock logs, and Module logs.

Operational Use

Revoke-Obfuscation has been used in numerous Mandiant investigations to identify obfuscated and non-obfuscated malicious PowerShell. It detects all obfuscation techniques in Invoke-Obfuscation, including two new techniques released with this presentation.

talks.title: Linux Stack Based V2X Framework
talks.teaser: Linux implementation of IEEE 802.11p and DSRC protocols enabling security research on V2X communications.
talks.summary:
Vehicle-to-Everything Communications

V2V and V2X wireless communications enable semi-autonomous driving through state information exchange between vehicles and infrastructure. Following 10+ years of standards development, implementation has lagged.

Standards and Development

The IEEE 802.11p and IEEE 1609 family standards define the protocol specifications. However, a lack of available implementations has prevented security community involvement in standards development and testing.

Vulnerability Analysis

Analysis of the WAVE/DSRC protocols reveals vulnerabilities that could render them unfit for safety-critical systems. These findings highlight the importance of early security research on emerging standards.

Linux Implementation

A complete Linux-stack implementation of IEEE 802.11p and IEEE 1609.3/4 is presented, providing hackers and academics with tools to participate in the engineering of secure standards for intelligent transportation systems.

talks.title: BITSInject
talks.teaser: Exploiting Windows BITS service state files to inject jobs and execute code as NT AUTHORITY/SYSTEM.
talks.summary:
Windows BITS Service

Windows' Background Intelligent Transfer Service (BITS) acts as a middleman for download jobs. From the moment a job is created, BITS manages the download lifecycle and handles queue management.

Vulnerability Discovery

Researchers discovered how BITS maintains its job queue using a state file on disk. The binary structure of this state file can be modified by local administrators to control jobs using special modifications to the file.

Exploitation Technique

By comprehending the binary structure of the state file, attackers can change job properties such as RemoteURL and Destination Path at runtime. They can also inject custom jobs without using BITS' public interfaces.

Code Execution

Combined with BITS' notification feature, this technique allows running arbitrary programs as the LocalSystem account within session 0. The researchers provide a one-click Python tool that performs the attack, SimpleBITSServer, and struct definition files for parsing BITS state files.

talks.title: Abusing Webhooks for Command and Control
talks.teaser: Establishing covert command and control through HTTP webhooks on approved business websites.
talks.summary:
Post-Exploitation Connectivity Challenge

Once inside a network, attackers need to exfiltrate data or execute commands on C2 servers. The problem is that outbound connectivity to C2 is often denied through DNS monitoring, ICMP blocking, and restricted cloud drive access.

Proxy and Filtering Evasion

Domain fronting for C2 may be ranked low by content proxies, restricting access to a handful of business websites. Traditional approaches trigger security alarms and reveal attacker presence.

Webhook-Based Solution

The technique uses HTTP callbacks (webhooks) to establish connectivity. Webhooks are used by organizations and can be leveraged as brokers for communication. Approved sites become communication channels, enabling data transfers and almost real-time command execution.

Implementation

Using approved sites as brokers allows bypassing strict defensive proxies and avoiding attribution. The tool released performs command-and-control communication through webhooks, fundamentally changing how attackers can maintain communication in restricted environments.

talks.title: Hacking the Cloud
talks.teaser: Leveraging domain access to pivot into target cloud deployments on Microsoft Azure and other providers.
talks.summary:
Domain-to-Cloud Pivot

Red teams often achieve deep domain access through traditional network compromise. However, many targets now have infrastructure in the cloud. Understanding how to follow when the path leads to cloud deployments is critical.

Cloud-Aware Penetration Testing

Red teams and penetration testers must think beyond traditional network boundaries and follow data and services into cloud environments. Azure remains the primary focus, but concepts apply to other cloud providers.

Attack Methodology

The talk focuses on taking domain access and leveraging internal access as a ticket to cloud deployments. Round-trip attacks from cloud to on-premises targets are discussed, including authorizations required to access cloud resources.

Microsoft Azure Focus

While largely focused on Azure implementations, the general approaches and attack patterns are applicable across most cloud providers. Understanding Azure-specific pivot points and authentication mechanisms is essential for modern penetration testing.

talks.title: The Black Art of Wireless Post Exploitation
talks.teaser: Bypassing port-based NAC with rogue access points to pivot past wireless perimeter defenses.
talks.summary:
Wireless Enterprise Security

Most forms of WPA2-EAP have been broken for nearly a decade. EAP-TTLS and EAP-PEAP remain susceptible to evil twin attacks, yet most enterprises rely on these technologies. The secure alternative, EAP-TLS, is arduous to implement.

NAC as Compensating Control

Organizations use port-based NAC appliances to prevent attackers from pivoting after wireless compromise. This approach assumes reactive security balances security and accessibility.

Assumption Challenge

A fundamental assumption is that EAP functions exclusively as perimeter defense. The presentation challenges this through a novel rogue access point attack that bypasses port-based access control mechanisms.

Pivoting Through Wireless

The attack demonstrates that reactive wireless security approaches are inadequate alternatives to strong physical layer protections like WPA2-EAP with EAP-TLS. Organizations must implement preventive controls, not rely on network segmentation after wireless compromise.

talks.title: Abusing Certificate Transparency Logs
talks.teaser: Exploiting CT logs to discover and attack web applications through their exposed certificates.
talks.summary:
Certificate Transparency System

The Certificate Transparency system provides public logs of TLS certificates. While primarily used to uncover certificate security issues, CT data has additional value for reconnaissance and exploitation.

Alternative Use Cases

Beyond security purposes, CT data can be exploited to discover common web applications. The presentation demonstrates novel ways to exploit these applications using Certificate Transparency information.

Targeting CMS Platforms

Common CMS platforms like WordPress, Joomla, and Typo3 can be discovered and targeted through CT log analysis. Understanding deployment patterns from certificate data enables targeted attacks.

Secure Standards Impact

Certificate Transparency has helped uncover incidents where certificate authorities violated rules. In September 2017, Google made CT mandatory for all new certificates, making this an opportune time to examine potential abuse vectors and help organizations understand attack possibilities.

talks.title: Call the plumber:  You have a leak in your named pipe
talks.teaser: Named pipes as application-level entry vectors for buffer overflows, DoS, and code injection attacks.
talks.summary:
Named Pipe Interface

Many security professionals are unfamiliar with the Windows named pipes interface or consider it internal-only. Open RPC (135) and SMB (445) ports are typically considered infrastructure penetration test entry points.

Application-Level Attack Surface

Named pipes can be used as application-level entry vectors for well-known attacks including buffer overflows, denial of service, and code injection attacks. XML bombs represent another attack class depending on listening service implementation.

Enterprise Application Exposure

Popular and widely-used Microsoft Windows enterprise applications open numerous named pipes on each endpoint or server. This significantly increases attack surface without organizational awareness. Limited mitigation options exist due to complete lack of awareness.

Discovery and Exploitation

The presentation highlights named pipes as a neglected external interface. Tools for finding vulnerable named pipes are demonstrated, along with mitigation strategies and exploitation processes on vulnerable applications, making named pipes an attractive target for sophisticated attackers.

talks.title: Evading next gen AV using AI
talks.teaser: AI agent using reinforcement learning to modify malware and evade ML-based antivirus detection.
talks.summary:
Next-Gen AV Approach

Next-generation antivirus relies on machine learning to generalize to never-before-seen malware. However, machine learning itself is susceptible to attack by other machine learning models.

Adversarial Machine Learning

The presentation demonstrates an AI agent trained through reinforcement learning to modify malware, enabling evasion of ML-based malware detection. Reinforcement learning has achieved superhuman performance in complex domains like Go and Atari games.

Malware Modification Strategy

The AI agent learns through thousands of games against a next-gen AV detector. It discovers functionality-preserving changes that can be applied to Windows PE malware files to bypass detection.

Accessibility

No machine learning background is required to understand the core concepts. Fundamental understanding of malware and Windows PE files is sufficient. The demonstration shows how AI can be used offensively to defeat AI-based defenses in antivirus products.

talks.title: The Adventures of AV and the Leaky Sandbox
talks.teaser: Cloud-based AV sandboxes can facilitate data exfiltration from high-security enterprise networks.
talks.summary:
High-Security Enterprise Challenge

Enterprises use cloud-enhanced antivirus for protection. Strict egress filtering prevents direct exfiltration, with endpoints having no direct Internet connection or only restricted connectivity.

Counterintuitive Risk

If malware already runs with full privileges on an endpoint, one might assume AV cannot degrade security. This assumption is completely wrong. Cloud-enhanced AV actually creates new exfiltration opportunities.

Sandbox Vulnerability

When cloud-enhanced AV employs an Internet-connected sandbox, it facilitates data exfiltration. Malware can leverage this sandbox to send data outside the enterprise, bypassing egress filtering controls.

Proof of Concept

The researchers demonstrate the technique with results from several prominent AV products. A tool implementing the exfiltration technique is released. Insights on AV in-the-cloud sandboxes and methods to enhance attacks are provided, along with possible mitigations for defenders.

talks.title: Are all BSDs are created equally? A survey of BSD kerne
talks.teaser: Comparative security audit of NetBSD, OpenBSD, and FreeBSD kernels to identify vulnerability patterns.
talks.summary:
Research Question

Given limited security kernel bug advisories released annually, the question arises: why are there so few BSD kernel bugs compared to other systems? Limited and outdated sources make this difficult to answer.

Audit Methodology

Active investigation and auditing is conducted across all 3 major BSD distributions: NetBSD, OpenBSD, and FreeBSD. Code review, fuzzing, and runtime testing target specific areas where bugs are likely to be found.

Research Process

Detailed investigation precedes thorough code review in candidate areas. Samples and demos illustrate findings. The presentation covers bug discovery methodology and results across the three distributions.

Comparative Analysis

The presentation identifies the clear winner and loser among BSD distributions based on bug findings. Code quality observations are detailed with pointers for improvement. The presentation answers the question of why so few kernel bug advisories exist compared to other operating systems.

talks.title: Groups Panel
talks.teaser: Insights from DEF CON's founder and group leaders on building local hacker communities worldwide.
talks.summary:
DEF CON Groups Program

DEF CON groups extend the DEF CON spirit year-round through local communities. Groups transcend borders, languages, and other separating factors.

Program Updates

Jayson E. Street, the Ambassador of DEF CON groups, discusses program updates and his global travel helping start groups around the world. The program's growth and evolution are covered.

Group Operations

Topics include what DEF CON groups are, how to get involved, and ideas for running groups. Location selection, spreading awareness, and community engagement strategies are discussed.

Group Projects

Group founders discuss awesome projects from their communities and share ideas for other groups. Projects range from custom badge builds to IoT devices, vintage gaming systems, custom routers, and smart home device hacking. These examples inspire local innovation and technical engagement.

talks.title: Introducing HUNT  Data Driven Web Hacking & Manual Testing
talks.teaser: Burp Suite extension using real-world assessment data to guide web hackers toward vulnerable parameters.
talks.summary:
Problem Statement

Web hacking relies on pure automation, which misses significant vulnerabilities. What if attackers had powerful alerts based on real threat intelligence about where vulnerabilities occur?

HUNT Solution

HUNT is a new Burp Suite extension providing parameter-level suggestions for vulnerability discovery. Rather than generic scanning, it uses data parsed from hundreds of real-world assessments.

Data-Driven Approach

HUNT guides web hackers toward vulnerable parameter patterns for SQLi, CMDi, LFI/RFI, and more. This data-driven design ensures more thorough target assessment beyond what pure automation achieves.

Methodology Integration

The extension organizes common web hacking methodologies inside Burp Suite. Open source design allows the security community to participate in improving detection capabilities. The tool bridges the gap between automated scanning and manual testing expertise.

talks.title: Wiping out CSRF
talks.teaser: Building practical CSRF protection solutions that work with legacy code and modern web applications.
talks.summary:
CSRF Problem Statement

CSRF remains elusive despite being well-known. Legacy code, legacy frameworks, and developer misunderstanding perpetuate vulnerabilities. Building solutions for any HTTP application is challenging.

Defense Primitives

The presentation introduces primitives and strategies for building CSRF solutions. Modern frameworks provide automatic solutions integrated into applications. However, many apps don't leverage these frameworks or use them incorrectly.

Comprehensive Protection

In-depth overview covers various reasons CSRF occurs and provides payload examples targeting specific issues and variations. Live demos show attacks and protections. Composing primitives into complete solutions addresses most CSRF cases.

Modern Solutions

Same Site Cookies represent a new extension potentially ending CSRF problems. The presentation shows how to layer prior solutions as graceful degradation for browsers not supporting modern mechanisms.

talks.title: Teaching Old Shellcode New Tricks
talks.teaser: Bypassing EMET and exploit mitigations to create improved Metasploit shellcode payloads.
talks.summary:
Shellcode Evolution

Metasploit x86 shellcode has been defeated by EMET and other techniques. These mitigations apply not only to exploit payloads but also to non-exploit situations like binary payload generation and PowerShell deployment.

Mitigation Techniques

The presentation describes taking Metasploit payloads and incorporating techniques to bypass Caller/EAF[+] checks that defend against post-ASLR/DEP bypass attempts.

Automation

These techniques are merged together with automation to improve overall effectiveness. The result is improved payload generation that overcomes modern exploit mitigations.

Practical Application

The approach allows using improved shellcode in various scenarios beyond traditional exploit development, making modern payloads effective despite layered mitigations.

talks.title: UnFucking Forensics: Active  Passive memory hacking   debugging
talks.teaser: Defensive and offensive memory hacking techniques for forensic analysis and covert attacker debugging.
talks.summary:
Forensic Challenges

The presentation covers how to perform forensics, counter-forensics, and defensive forensic improvement. Understanding return-oriented programming (ROP) and static detection from memory is critical.

Defensive Techniques

WTF is ROP and why it matters. Detecting RoP statically from memory and counteracting Gargoyle attacks provides defense insights. These techniques help incident responders and forensic analysts.

Memory Debugging

In-memory passive debugging techniques allow covert debugging of attackers. The term "active passive" indicates methods not using easily detectable events or techniques that attackers would notice.

Offensive Techniques

CloudLeech represents a cloud-based twist on Ulf Frisk Direct Memory Attack. Offensive and defensive capabilities provide comprehensive view of memory-based attack and defense mechanisms.

talks.title: There’s no place like 127.001: Achieving reliable DNS rebinding
talks.teaser: Bypassing browser protections and network mitigations to reliably exploit local network services.
talks.summary:
Trust Assumptions

People lock doors at night but rarely bolt furniture to floors. Similarly, developers treat local networks as trusted without implementing proper authentication. This assumption is dangerous.

DNS Rebinding Attacks

Same-origin policy assumes internal HTTP traffic is trusted. DNS rebinding bypasses this by exploiting implicit trust in local networks. Older techniques have been largely dismissed as unreliable.

Overcoming Limitations

The presentation covers DNS rebinding mechanics, browser mitigations, network defenses, and how to bypass each. The notorious unreliability that causes developers to ignore the issue is resolved through proper technique.

Practical Exploitation

Analysis of popular services shows how they are affected by DNS rebinding. A released tool automates attack generation and mitigation bypass. Live demonstration exploits vulnerable services to achieve remote code execution, proving practical exploit value.

talks.title: Get $pwnd: Attacking Battle Hardened Windows Server
talks.teaser: Systematically destroying hardened PowerShell JEA endpoints through insecure coding practices.
talks.summary:
PowerShell JEA Hardening

Windows Server has introduced advanced remote management hardening through PowerShell Just Enough Administration (JEA). Correctly configured hardened JEA endpoints provide formidable barriers against attackers with whitelisted commands and no OS-level access.

Attack Methodology

The presentation shows systematic destruction of hardened JEA endpoints. Exploiting insecure coding practices and administrative complexity reveals weaknesses in otherwise strong hardening.

Bypass Techniques

When JEA is properly configured, attackers must exploit implementation weaknesses and command functionality misuse. The techniques show how proper hardening can still be circumvented.

Practical Demonstration

Live demonstrations showcase the attack process, illustrating how organizations can identify and eliminate the exploited weaknesses in their JEA implementations.

talks.title: Gaining persistency by abusing advanced authe
talks.teaser: Lesser-known persistence mechanisms using Kerberos delegation and advanced authentication abuse.
talks.summary:
Persistence Challenge

Credentials remain favorite targets for advanced attackers, allowing efficient network traversal without exploits. Achieving persistency requires advanced evasion techniques to remain undetected even after discovery.

Traditional Techniques

Past persistency methods using local accounts, Group Policy Objects (GPOs), and skeleton key attacks are discussed and analyzed for modern insufficiency.

Advanced Mechanisms

Comprehensive analysis covers lesser-known persistence mechanisms using non-mainstream methods. Object manipulation and Kerberos delegation represent sophisticated approaches unavailable to casual attackers.

Defensive Strategies

The presentation shows how defenders can secure their environments against advanced persistence threats. Understanding these sophisticated techniques is critical for both offense and defense.

talks.title: CableTap: Wirelessly Tapping Home Networks
speakers: Marc Newlin, Logan Lamb, Chris Grayson
talks.teaser: Critical vulnerabilities in ISP-provided gateways enabling wireless interception of all network traffic.
talks.summary:
ISP Gateway Vulnerabilities

Critical vulnerabilities in RDK-based wireless gateways and set-top boxes from vendors including Cisco, Arris, Technicolor, and Motorola impact millions of ISP customers.

Remote Exploitation

Research shows that it was possible to remotely and wirelessly tap all Internet and voice traffic passing through affected gateways. Without direct Internet access, attackers can impersonate legitimate ISP customers and access public hotspots.

Multiple Attack Vectors

Root shell access can be gained through methods beyond traditional web vulnerabilities. Options include generating hidden Wi-Fi network passphrases and logging into web UIs with hard-coded credentials.

Vendor Response

The presentation covers technical specifics of exploits discovered. Remediation actions taken by affected vendors and guidance for users is provided. Attack chain examples demonstrate real-world exploitation impact.

talks.title: Radio Exploitation 101
talks.teaser: Fundamentals of wireless protocol exploitation using software-defined and hardware radios.
talks.summary:
Vulnerable Wireless Protocols

Dallas tornado siren attacks, hacked electric skateboards, and insecure smart door locks share a common thread: vulnerable wireless protocols. RF protocol exploitation grows increasingly common due to mobile and IoT proliferation.

RF Fundamentals

The presentation introduces essential RF concepts and characteristics. Non-Wi-Fi and non-Bluetooth RF protocols remain mysterious to many security practitioners, but exploiting them is surprisingly accessible.

Wireless Threat Taxonomy

Different attack methods are analyzed and classified. Parallels to wired network exploits highlight familiar patterns, while unique RF attack primitives are introduced.

Practical Demonstrations

Each attack is shown in practice using software-defined and hardware radios. Attendees learn exploitation mechanics and how to bridge IP network exploitation skills into the wireless domain.

talks.title: Amateur Digital Archeology
talks.teaser: Using digital forensics techniques to recover history and data from vintage hardware artifacts.
talks.summary:
Digital Archeology Concept

'Digital Archeology' is a digital forensics text book topic. Applying forensics techniques from cyber crime investigations to address void in archeology relating to digital media and silicon artifacts opens new possibilities.

NYC Resistor Projects

At NYC Resistor in Brooklyn, digital archeology projects have been conducted on several occasions, providing enjoyable and educational experiences.

Shuttle Laptop Discovery

The speaker purchased a laptop at auction claiming to be from a Space Shuttle Mission. The device proved mostly authentic. The presentation details what was discovered about the device's history and recovery techniques used.

Findings

Extensive information about the authentic shuttle hardware was recovered. Notably, the sister laptop with matching serial numbers may have been discovered, providing additional historical artifacts for analysis.

talks.title: Taking Windows 10 Kernel Exploitation to the next level
talks.teaser: Novel KASLR bypasses and kernel pool exploitation to achieve code execution despite Windows 10 hardening.
talks.summary:
Windows 10 Hardening

Since Windows 10 release and especially in Anniversary and Creators Updates, Microsoft introduced powerful exploit mitigations including full-scale KASLR and blocking of kernel pointer leaks.

Kernel Primitives

The presentation reviews powerful read and write kernel primitives that work despite recent hardening. Window and Bitmap object abuse provides generic approaches to leveraging write-what-where vulnerabilities.

KASLR Bypass

Previously unknown KASLR bypasses in Windows 10 Creators Update are disclosed. Kernel driver leaks provide initial information, but novel de-randomization techniques work without relying on direct driver attacks.

Code Execution

Obtaining kernel-mode code execution requires overcoming Page Table Entry randomization. Dynamic reverse engineering provides one de-randomization approach. Alternatively, arbitrary-size executable kernel pool memory allocation enables code execution transfer through hijacked system calls.

talks.title: macOS:iOS Kernel Debugging and Heap Feng Shui
talks.teaser: Kernel debugging techniques and heap feng shui methods for iOS and macOS kernel exploitation.
talks.summary:
Kernel Debugging Challenges

Kernel bugs are difficult to reproduce and often cause system panic. Kernel debugging is necessary for panic analysis, but kernel code cannot execute in debuggers, making tracking difficult.

macOS Kernel Debugging Kit

macOS provides powerful kernel debugging through KDK (Kernel Development Kit). This tool assists in analyzing panic scenes and developing kernel exploits.

iOS Kernel Debugging

While iOS lacks official kernel debugger, kernel debugging is still possible through leveraging tricks and techniques. The presentation shares kernel debugging methods specific to latest iOS/macOS versions.

Heap Mitigations and Bypass

New kernel heap mitigation mechanisms on iOS 10/macOS 10.12 are analyzed. Two novel heap feng shui techniques bypass these mitigations. Concrete kernel heap overflow bug debugging demonstrates leveraging new heap feng shui to gain arbitrary kernel memory read/write on iOS 10.2/macOS 10.12.

talks.title: Hacking travel routers like it's 1999
talks.teaser: Discovering and exploiting memory corruption in HooToo travel routers despite exploitation mitigations.
talks.summary:
Digital Nomad Security

Traveling security researchers need internet safety like anyone else. The HooToo TM06 travel router was purchased to create a secure internet enclave while traveling globally.

Vulnerability Discovery

Fuzzing and reverse engineering revealed severe memory corruption vulnerabilities. Despite employing exploitation mitigations, the device lacks critical protections like NX-Stack/Heap and canaries.

Exploitation Bypass

Two memory corruption vulnerabilities are exploited to achieve arbitrary shellcode execution. Mitigation bypass techniques show what protections should have been employed but were missing.

IoT Security Implications

The research highlights the poor security state of IoT devices like travel routers. Detailed methodology for discovering and exploiting embedded systems is valuable for security of IoT and MIPS-based devices.

talks.title: XenoScan  Scanning Memory Like a Boss
talks.teaser: Advanced memory scanning tool for detecting complex data structures and class instances in memory.
talks.summary:
Memory Scanning Evolution

XenoScan is next-generation tooling for game hackers. Building on Cheat Engine and Tsearch foundations, XenoScan makes innovations in memory scanning capabilities.

Advanced Features

The tool can scan for partial structures and detect complex data structures like binary trees and linked lists. Class-instances on the heap are identified and grouped by type.

Extensibility

Extensibility allows working with native processes and games running in emulators. The tool's flexibility makes it useful for day-to-day reverse engineering and hacking workflows beyond game modification.

Technical Details

Low-level implementation details explain how smart memory scanning works and why it's effective. Open-source development via interactive livestream allows community participation in future development and feature additions.

talks.title: Nathan Seidle -Open Source Safe Cracking Robots: Combinations Under 1 Hour
talks.teaser: $200 open source robot that cracks combination safes by measuring internal bits and set testing.
talks.summary:
Safe Cracking Challenge

Combination safes provide security through mechanical complexity. A low-cost robotic approach reduces crack times to under an hour through measurement and testing techniques.

Robot Design

Using a motor with high-count encoder, the robot takes measurements of internal bits while the safe remains closed. Measurements expose one combination digit.

Set Testing Method

'Set testing' is a novel method created to decrease time between combination attempts. This technique dramatically improves attack efficiency.

Technology Stack

With 3D printing, Arduino, and powerful magnets, the robot cracks most fire safes. Live cracking demonstrations during the talk showcase practical real-world effectiveness of the approach.

talks.title: PEIMA Using Power Laws to address Denial of Service Attacks
talks.teaser: Mathematical approach using power laws to detect DoS attacks and other anomalous network activity.
talks.summary:
Denial of Service Problem

DoS attacks require low resources and knowledge, are easy to deploy, and remain remarkably effective. Understanding attack patterns is critical for defense.

PEIMA Method

PEIMA is a novel approach to client-side malicious activity detection using mathematical laws typically applied in finance, text retrieval, and social media analysis. The method is fast and accurate.

Capabilities

PEIMA determines when DoS attacks start and stop without erroneously flagging legitimate heavy server interest. Beyond DoS, unusual activity metrics help detect intrusions and asset compromise.

Network Monitoring

Identifying anomalous network and user metrics provides defense advantages. The technique helps organizations understand and defend against various forms of network-based attacks.

talks.title: Digital Vengeance  Exploiting the Most Notorious C&C Toolki
talks.teaser: Exploring how to make an internet that improves society through code, business, lawsuits, and legislation.
talks.summary:
Complex Questions

Is Net Neutrality rising or falling? Is DRM rising or falling? Will crypto be banned, and if it wins, will its application be ransomware or revolution? Is history bending toward justice or snapping toward barbarism?

The Answer: It's Complicated

These are complex questions without simple answers. Understanding involves examining multiple forces shaping internet evolution.

Making Better Internet

A better world isn't a product; it's a process. The right question isn't whether the internet makes us better or worse, but how we make an internet that improves the world.

Multiple Levers

Improvement comes through code, but also conversations, businesses, lawsuits, and legislation. Moving in the right direction toward a better world means understanding all these levers and how to apply them effectively.

talks.title: A Picture is Worth a Thousand Words, Literally
talks.teaser: AI-powered steganography hiding data in social network images beyond human visual perception.
talks.summary:
Digital Media Communication

Images, videos, and digital media provide convenient communication through social networks. Broadcasting capability and information richness enable both legitimate and illicit uses.

Image Steganography

JPEG files can disguise foreign data through minor pixel and metadata alterations. Covert messages in billions of daily posted images might be possible, but scale automation faces technical challenges.

Neural Network Learning

Convolutional neural networks learn to reverse-engineer transformations applied by social networks. The network optimizes hidden data capacity by identifying pixels and metadata least modified during platform processing.

Data Acquisition and Results

Social networks provide free bulk upload/download for training data. Experiments show hidden data transmission through social images with high fidelity, demonstrating AI can hide data in plain sight at scale beyond human detection despite third-party manipulation and compression.

talks.title: Demystifying Windows Kernel Exploitation by Abusing GDI Objects
talks.teaser: Complete walkthroughs of Windows kernel exploitation using GDI bitmap objects with released exploits.
talks.summary:
Kernel Exploitation Challenge

Windows kernel exploitation is difficult to learn due to limited walkthroughs. Full exploitation process documentation is rare but necessary for skill development.

GDI Object Abuse

The presentation provides detailed steps for developing privilege escalation exploits. GDI bitmap objects provide abuse vectors for achieving kernel code execution.

Exploit Development Process

Reversing Microsoft patches, identifying bugs, developing PoCs, and turning them into code execution demonstrates complete exploitation methodology. Complete exploitation processes are rare and valuable.

Released Exploits

A Windows 8.1 x64 exploit using GDI bitmap objects is released. A previously unreleased Windows 7 SP1 x86 exploit using novel GDI object abuse techniques is also provided, advancing the field.

talks.title: Microservices and FaaS for Offensive Security
talks.teaser: Scaling offensive security testing using serverless functions and distributed cloud infrastructure.
talks.summary:
Serverless Computing

Cloud providers offer serverless or Function-as-a-Service platforms for rapid application deployment without dedicated servers. These platforms enable scaling of time-consuming offensive security tasks.

Scaling Opportunities

Attacks previously impractical due to time and resource constraints become feasible. Cloud services provide unlimited scaling with public IP addresses for attribution avoidance.

Offensive Applications

Undetected port scans against short-lived services, brute-force attacks on services and OTP values, and opportunistic attacks benefit from cloud scaling. Custom databases like Shodan/Censys and IPv6 exploration become practical.

Guide and Demonstrations

The presentation provides a guide for scaling offensive tools and demonstrates practical benefits of cloud services. Attendees learn how cloud platforms can enable sophisticated offensive testing previously limited by resources.

talks.title: WSUSpendu: How to hang WSUS clients
talks.teaser: Exploiting WSUS update infrastructure to control targeted systems from a compromised domain.
talks.summary:
Post-Compromise Challenge

After owning a domain controller, compromising targeted systems should be straightforward. However, targets deeper in networks may be inaccessible through filtering.

WSUS Opportunity

Target domains pulling updates from WSUS servers controlled by the attacker create opportunity. Unfortunately, available tools don't work if network architecture prevents network attacks.

Novel Approach

A new approach circumvents limitations, allowing circumventing this problem. The attack exploits vulnerable architectures, allowing controlled update delivery.

Tools and Mitigations

Public tooling demonstrates the attack with in-context demonstrations. The presentation also explains vulnerable architectures and describes how to protect update infrastructure against similar attacks and air-gap scenarios.

talks.title: Koadic C: Windows COM Command & Control Framework
talks.teaser: Post-exploitation tool using COM objects and Windows Script Host with compatibility to Windows 2000.
talks.summary:
COM-Based Post Exploitation

Koadic C3 is a Windows post-exploitation tool similar to Meterpreter and PowerShell Empire. The key difference is using Windows Script Host (JScript/VBScript) for operations.

Wide Compatibility

Compatibility spans from Windows 2000 without service packs to Windows 10. COM object availability on all versions enables universal deployment.

COM Object Exploration

Default COM objects provide large, underexplored attack surface. Numerous Windows scripting quirks with interesting workarounds were discovered during development.

Capabilities

Payloads serve completely in memory from stage 0 onward. Cryptographically secure communications over SSL/TLS work depending on victim OS availability. Multiple fork-to-shellcode methods work despite traditional limitations. Development builds on work by engima0x3, subTee, and other researchers.

talks.title: Application DoS In Microservice Architectures
talks.teaser: Application-layer DoS targeting expensive service calls to cause cascading microservice failures.
talks.summary:
Service Instability Attack

Application DDoS represents one of the most devastating ways to cause service instability in modern microservice architectures. Unlike network DDoS, application DoS targets expensive calls within architectures.

Microservice Relationships

Complex interconnected relationships between services enable attacking the system's own infrastructure. Legitimate-looking requests pass web application firewalls while causing exponential service load.

Behavior Analysis

Netflix application security team identified areas enabling exponential-work attacks. Single API requests fan out through infrastructure causing cascading dependent service calls with massive effect.

Framework and Demonstration

Frameworks refined automation and reproducibility of endpoint testing. Live demonstrations against production environments show architectural and technical approaches for identifying and remediating application DDoS vulnerabilities. Open sourced frameworks enable organization-wide testing.

talks.title: Exploiting 0ld Mag stripe information with New technology
talks.teaser: Using audio transmission and Bluetooth to spoof magstripe data and perform mass card attacks.
talks.summary:
Magstripe Legacy

Magnetic stripe technology remains in use despite modern alternatives. Private companies, banks, trains, subways, hotels, and schools use magstripe for transactions, access control, and new protocols like MST.

Historical Challenges

Malicious spoofing was historically slow and difficult. Brute force attacks were tedious and time-consuming, making massive attacks impractical.

Modern Attack Feasibility

Technology like Bluetooth makes persistent attacks against multiple readers simultaneously practical. Audio transmission of magstripe data enables fast, easy cross-platform spoofing.

Attack Applications

Attackers can transmit audio spoof information to many readers simultaneously through audio spoofing and Bluetooth. Magstripe jamming against credit card terminals and PoS systems becomes practical. Hotel door locks and tokenization processes are vulnerable to brute force attacks enabled by new technology.

talks.title: Exploiting Continuous Integration (CI) and Automated Build systems
talks.teaser: Discovering and exploiting CI/CD build system vulnerabilities for container compromise and persistence.
talks.summary:
CI/CD Infrastructure

Continuous Integration has revolutionized development through automation of code builds, tests, and deployments. This saves time and resources while enabling rapid deployment.

Security Implications

Sudden demand for CI systems drove adoption of practices with large security implications, especially for internally hosted systems.

Automated Testing and Exploitation

A tool automates offensive testing against popular CI systems. Web hook initiation provides attack vectors, especially for public code repository changes.

Exploration and Demonstration

The presentation overviews popular CI tools and security benefits. Specific vulnerability examples show exploitation opportunities. Tools demonstrate capability to exploit CI implementations, establish persistence, and achieve command and control in vulnerable build containers. Modular design facilitates exploration of additional CI products and exploitation concepts.

talks.title: Trey Forgety - Inside the “Meet Desai” Attack Defending Distributed Targets
talks.teaser: In-depth analysis of the 2016 DTDoS attacks against 9-1-1 centers and defenses against telecom attacks.
talks.summary:
DTDoS Attack

In October 2016, a teenage hacker triggered DTDoS attacks against 9-1-1 centers across the United States with just five lines of code and a tweet. This attack highlighted critical infrastructure vulnerabilities.

Attack Analysis

The presentation provides in-depth analysis of the attack mechanics and impact. Latest academic works on TDoS attacks directed at 9-1-1 systems are reviewed and critiqued.

Mitigation Strategies

Potential mitigation strategies for legacy TDM and future all-IP access networks are discussed. Both access network providers and originating service providers need mitigation approaches.

Infrastructure Defense

Over-the-top originating services and dependent devices require protection strategies. Understanding DTDoS attack patterns is critical for protecting emergency services infrastructure from both traditional and emerging threats.

talks.title: Game of Chromes: Owning the Web with Zombie Chrome Extensions
talks.teaser: Compromising Chrome extensions and web stores to create browser botnets through extension vulnerabilities.
talks.summary:
Extension Bot Attacks

In April 2016, malicious bots attacked Wix servers, creating accounts and publishing websites in mass. A malicious Chrome extension on tens of thousands of devices enabled the attack. Distribution via Facebook messaging extended its reach.

Elusive Bot Nature

These extension bots highly elude detection, especially web-based bot-detection systems. Legitimate extensions perform similar actions like sending Facebook messages and creating websites.

XSS in Extensions

Recently, popular Chrome extensions were found vulnerable to XSS. Remarkably, extensions suffer XSS like web applications, but impact is much deadlier. Adobe Acrobat extension's DOM-based XSS allowed control on 30 million devices.

Zombie Extensions

Extension XSS flaws lead to permanent browser control, turning extensions into zombies. Similar techniques to 2016 Wix/Facebook attacks enable efficient malicious payload distribution through social platforms, creating powerful web botnets.

talks.title: Malicious CDNs
talks.teaser: Discovering botnet and bulletproof hosting infrastructure through anomalous SSL certificate patterns.
talks.summary:
SSL Analysis

Prior research examined relationships between malware, bulletproof hosting, and SSL using seed domains. Novel statistical techniques discover botnet and bulletproof hosting IP space by examining SSL distribution patterns.

Open Source Data

Using only open source datasets and tools, infrastructure discovery becomes possible with limited seed information. IPv4 namespace scanning produces 4 million node bipartite graphs connecting common names to IP/CIDR/ASN.

Relative Entropy Metric

Relative entropy creates pairwise distance metrics between common names and ASNs. The metric generalizes regular and anomalous SSL distribution patterns, identifying domains with anomalous structures.

Zbot Proxy Discovery

Zbot proxy network structure parallels popular CDNs like Akamai and Google but uses compromised devices. Layering SSL signals with passive DNS data extracts Zbot domains with high accuracy, enabling infrastructure discovery.

talks.title: Closing Ceremonies
talks.teaser: Closing remarks and celebration from DEF CON 25, reflecting on the conference and community.
talks.summary:
Conference: Closing Ceremonies. Conference closing or opening ceremony.

(AI summary — Claude Haiku)

talks.title: Welcome
talks.teaser: Opening address welcoming attendees to DEF CON 25 conference.
talks.summary:
### Celebrating 25 Years of Hacker Culture
At 00:00, Jeff Moss (The Dark Tangent) takes the main stage to welcome attendees to DEF CON 25, commemorating a quarter-century since he founded the conference in 1993. Moss reflects on DEF CON's humble beginnings as a 100-person farewell party for a friend in Las Vegas, marveling at how it evolved into the world's premier hacker convention, gathering over 25,000 security professionals, researchers, students, and hobbyists.

### From Underground Subculture to Strategic Advisory
At 04:20 and 07:38, Moss reflects on the monumental cultural transformation of the cybersecurity landscape over the preceding 25 years. In the early 1990s, hackers were viewed with deep skepticism, suspicion, and legal hostility by corporations and law enforcement. Today, global policymakers, intelligence leaders, and Fortune 500 executives actively seek the advice of the hacker community to secure critical national infrastructure, guide international technology legislation, and design resilient digital systems.

### The Expansion of Community Villages and Specialized Tracks
At 09:15, Moss outlines the physical and conceptual reorganization of the conference to accommodate its explosive growth across Caesars Palace, the Flamingo, and neighboring venues. He emphasizes the critical role of specialized Villages—including the Packet Hacking Village, IoT Village, Car Hacking Village, and Biohacking Village—which allow attendees to immerse themselves in hands-on hardware hacking, capture-the-flag competitions, and domain-specific research.

### Preserving Hacker Ethos and Community Integrity
Concluding between 11:30 and 13:45, Moss delivers an impassioned reminder of the values that define DEF CON. Despite corporate sponsorships, mainstream media attention, and government attendance, DEF CON remains fundamentally defined by individual curiosity, ethical inquiry, mentorship, and a vibrant counterculture. He encourages attendees to step outside their technical comfort zones, embrace live music and contest events, and carry the spirit of open learning forward into the next quarter-century.

(AI summary — Gemini 3.8 Flash)

talks.title: Conference - Alvaro Muñoz, Alexandr Mirosh - Friday the 13th JSON attacks
talks.teaser: Remote code execution vulnerabilities in JSON parsers across .NET and Java libraries.
talks.summary:
Java Deserialization Crisis

2016 was the year of Java deserialization apocalypse. Apache Commons Collection RCE gadget brought attention to forgotten vulnerabilities, motivating security fixes across the community.

JSON Migration

A suggested solution was migrating from Java Deserialization to safer JSON formats. Popular JSON parsers in .NET and Java are analyzed for RCE vectors.

Vulnerable Libraries

RCE is possible in these libraries, with analysis showing default vulnerable configurations. Discussion covers common configurations enabling additional library vulnerabilities.

Beyond Deserialization

JSON parsers, considered safer alternatives, still exhibit serious vulnerabilities. Understanding JSON parsing security is critical for moving beyond deserialization while maintaining security.

talks.title: Everything to know about Android packers
talks.teaser: Comprehensive overview of Android packers and techniques to unpack and analyze packed applications.
talks.summary:
Android Packer Industry

Understanding the Android ecosystem requires understanding Android packers. Whether protecting legitimate app business logic or hiding malware, packer usage is on the rise.

Packer Tactics

Packers employ elaborate tactics to prevent reverse engineers and static analysis engines from understanding app contents. State-of-the-art ELF tampering, obfuscation, and anti-debugging techniques are employed.

Packer Analysis

Overview of the packer industry and real-world test cases are provided. Deep technical dive into internal workings of popular Android packers exposes protection methods.

Countermeasures

Various techniques circumvent packers, allowing hackers and security researchers to unpack secrets. Understanding packer internals enables bypassing protections and analyzing protected applications.

talks.title: Persisting with Microsoft Office  Abusing Extensibility Options
talks.teaser: Six Office-based persistence mechanisms using add-ins and extensibility features.
talks.summary:
Microsoft Office Persistence

Microsoft Office is nearly ubiquitous on compromised workstations. Native Office functionality provides multiple persistence opportunities for red teamers.

Persistence Mechanisms

Six persistence mechanisms are discussed: WLL/XLL add-ins for Word/Excel (legacy DLL loading), VBA add-ins for Excel/PowerPoint, COM add-ins for all Office products, Automation add-ins for Excel, VBE add-ins for VBA products, and VSTO add-ins for all products.

Comparative Analysis

Each mechanism's advantages and disadvantages for red teamers are discussed. Complexity, privilege requirements, and VDI applicability inform mechanism selection.

Defense Perspective

Approaches for detection and prevention of Office persistence mechanisms are covered. Threat hunters and incident responders gain detection strategies for identifying Office-based persistence implants.

talks.title: Assembly Language is Too High Level
talks.teaser: Demonstrating that x86 assembly instructions have multiple valid machine-code representations.
talks.summary:
Assembly and Machine Code

Assembly language is often described as one-to-one with machine code, but this is incorrect. Assembly instructions can have multiple valid machine-code representations.

Redundant Encoding

Single assembly instructions can encode as different machine code bytes, and different machine code can decode to equivalent instructions. Understanding these redundancies reveals security implications.

IRASM Tool

The Interactive Redundant Assembler (irasm) is released, allowing exploration of alternate machine-code representations. Tool output can be used in tools like mona for self-modifying code and exploitation.

Applications

Use cases include creating alternate shellcode representations, improving tool flexibility, and applying stego techniques. Understanding machine-code redundancy provides additional options for sophisticated exploitation and evasion.

talks.title: Cisco Catalyst Exploitation
talks.teaser: Exploitation development for critical Cisco Catalyst switch vulnerabilities enabling full device control.
talks.summary:
Cisco Security Announcement

In March 2017, Cisco announced that over 300 switch models were vulnerable to critical vulnerabilities allowing full device control. This vulnerability was coupled with Vault 7 disclosures about tools for accessing network equipment.

RemediationChallenge

Patching thousands of different switch models is a massive undertaking. Patched versions were announced on May 8, 2017, but deployment remains ongoing.

Exploit Development

The presentation details exploit development for Cisco Cluster Management Protocol vulnerabilities. Despite exploit mitigations like DEP and ASLR, the attack surfaces exist and are exploitable.

Hardening Assessment

Network equipment is often assumed to be more hardened than end systems. Research demonstrates that finding critical vulnerabilities and developing working exploits is feasible through systematic analysis and reverse engineering of the vulnerability.

talks.title: Conference - Josh Schwartz, John Cramb
talks.teaser: Open source modular framework for creating malware implants and automating C2 infrastructure.
talks.summary:
Operational Challenges

Red teamers and offensive security operators face overhead of fighting attribution, spinning infrastructure, and rewriting malware. This operational burden is a significant time sink.

MEATPISTOL Framework

MEATPISTOL is a modular malware framework for implant creation, infrastructure automation, and shell interaction. Designed for offensive security operators requiring rapid configuration and long-lived implant deployment.

Capabilities

The framework enables efficient yoloscoped adversarial campaigns against capable targets. Moving beyond one-off malware toward framework-based development improves operational efficiency.

Open Source Release

The framework is publicly released as open source, enabling the security community to benefit from the design and contribute improvements. The project provides infrastructure automation and efficient implant development for red teamers.

talks.title: Designing Active Directory DACL Backdoors
talks.teaser: Using Active Directory DACL misconfigurations to achieve domain compromise and persistence.
talks.summary:
Active Directory Security

Active Directory object discretionary access control lists (DACLs) represent an untapped offensive landscape, often overlooked by attackers and defenders. Control relationships between AD objects align with "attackers think in graphs" philosophy.

Control Edges

DACL analysis exposes previously unseen control edges, dramatically expanding paths to complete domain compromise. Attackers can identify numerous paths through careful DACL analysis.

Persistence Opportunity

DACL misconfigurations provide covert persistence deployment opportunities. Distinguishing intentional configurations from accidents is difficult, providing plausible deniability.

Forensic Analysis

Active Directory DACL backdoors have minimal forensic footprint and maximum plausible deniability. Understanding DACL-based control relationships and covert persistence techniques is critical for both offensive and defensive security.

talks.title: The Brain's Last Stand
talks.teaser: Former world chess champion Garry Kasparov reflects on his matches against Deep Blue and explores collaborative strategies for human and machine intelligence.
talks.summary:
Reflections on the Watershed 1997 Match

Twenty years after his historic chess match against the IBM supercomputer Deep Blue, former World Chess Champion Garry Kasparov evaluates the evolution of artificial intelligence and machine capabilities. The match marked a pivotal turning point in public perception, cementing the concept of human versus machine competition in the global consciousness while illustrating the raw computational power of specialized heuristic evaluation.

Moving Beyond the Man Versus Machine Dichotomy

Kasparov challenges both extreme utopian predictions and pessimistic dystopian warnings regarding technological unemployment and societal displacement. Rather than viewing machine intelligence as an adversarial replacement for human agency, he advocates an integration model where human intuition and strategic judgment augment automated computational processes.

Human Plus Machine Collaboration

Drawing on two decades of competitive chess experimentation with Advanced Chess and freestyle tournaments, Kasparov demonstrates that a moderately skilled human player paired with an ordinary computer program consistently outperforms both unassisted grandmasters and standalone supercomputers. The decisive factor is not the superior brilliance of the human or the raw speed of the machine, but the efficiency of the interface and collaborative workflow established between them.

Navigating the Automation Revolution

Addressing anxieties surrounding workforce automation and economic disruption, the talk emphasizes that technological progress routinely obsoletes routine tasks while creating opportunities for higher-level problem solving. Kasparov argues that resisting technological adoption is futile, urging security researchers, technologists, and policymakers to embrace the AI revolution by cultivating adaptable skills and designing transparent decision-support systems.

talks.title: Open Source Safe Cracking Robots
talks.teaser: Demonstrates an open-source robotic rig built with Arduino and 3D-printed parts that measures internal wheel tolerances to crack combination fire safes in under an hour.
talks.summary:
Low-Cost Physical Security Auditing

Mechanical combination safes are commonly deployed in commercial and residential settings under the assumption that non-destructive brute-force attacks require prohibitive amounts of time. Nathan Seidle demonstrates a low-cost, open-source automated safe-cracking robotic platform fabricated using off-the-shelf 3D-printed components, an Arduino microcontroller, and standard stepper motors totaling approximately two hundred dollars.

Measuring Internal Wheel Pack Tolerances

Instead of blindly attempting all possible numerical combinations across the three-wheel or four-wheel pack, the robot uses a motor coupled with an optical encoder to measure mechanical resistance and wheel contact points while the safe remains closed. By measuring subtle rotational discrepancies when the dial interacts with internal drive pins, the system can reliably isolate one of the combination digits, dramatically reducing the remaining mathematical search space.

Optimizing Dialing with Set Testing

Standard dialing methods require resetting the entire wheel pack between attempts, consuming valuable seconds per trial. Seidle introduces a specialized search algorithm called set testing that groups potential number combinations into continuous sweeps, minimizing unnecessary reverse revolutions and reducing total cracking time to under sixty minutes on standard fire-resistant safes.

Open Source Hardware and Attack Demos

The complete schematics, 3D models, and Arduino firmware are released open-source to allow physical security professionals and penetration testers to audit safe vulnerabilities. Live demonstrations illustrate the physical mounting mechanism using high-strength neodymium magnets, automated dial calibration, and the precise mechanical retraction of the locking bolt upon discovering the final combination.

talks.title: Jailbreaking Apple Watch
talks.teaser: Explores watchOS security architecture and demonstrates jailbreaking Apple Watch by bypassing codesigning, sandboxing, and kernel memory protections.
talks.summary:
Wearable Platform Security Architecture

The Apple Watch and its dedicated operating system watchOS handle sensitive biometric, navigational, and communication data while maintaining tight pairing with companion iOS devices. Max Bazaliy examines the core security architecture implemented in watchOS, including mandatory code signature enforcement, application sandboxing, privilege separation, and kernel-level memory protections designed to prevent unauthorized code execution.

Auditing watchOS and iOS Attack Surfaces

Because watchOS shares extensive architectural lineage with Darwin and iOS, vulnerabilities in common subsystem services—such as CoreAnimation, Bluetooth pairing daemons, and system kernel drivers—can be leveraged against the wearable device. Bazaliy identifies attack surfaces accessible over local wireless transport protocols and analyzes how vulnerabilities can be triggered within system daemon contexts.

Chaining Exploits for Kernel Execution

Achieving a functional jailbreak requires constructing a multi-stage exploitation chain. The attack initiates through an application or media parsing bug to gain initial userland execution, followed by a sandbox escape that targets local inter-process communication services. Finally, a kernel vulnerability is exploited to defeat Kernel Address Space Layout Randomization (KASLR) and overwrite memory management registers to disable code signing validation.

Impact and Device Post-Exploitation

With kernel privileges established on the Apple Watch, the jailbreak demonstrates direct access to sensitive local sqlite databases containing message archives, contact lists, GPS coordinates, and health telemetry. Bazaliy details debugging hooks and instrumentation frameworks that enable researchers to audit previously inaccessible watchOS internal daemons and assess wearable security posture.

talks.title: How We Created the First SHA-1 Collision
talks.teaser: Recounts the computation and cryptanalytic engineering behind the SHAttered project that produced the first practical SHA-1 collision.
talks.summary:
The Theoretical Demise of SHA-1

The cryptographic hash function SHA-1 was designed by the National Security Agency in 1995 and widely integrated into digital certificate standards, version control systems, and document signing protocols. While theoretical differential path attacks were published by Xiaoyun Wang and colleagues in 2005, practical generation of an identical hash digest from two distinct meaningful files remained computationally intractable for over a decade.

The SHAttered Project Architecture

Elie Bursztein details the collaborative research initiative between Google and CWI Amsterdam that produced the first practical SHA-1 collision, known as the SHAttered attack. The attack required calculating approximately nine quintillion SHA-1 operations, representing an unprecedented distributed computation across heterogeneous CPU clusters and specialized GPU acceleration nodes optimized for cryptanalytic round-reduction algorithms.

Generating Valid Colliding PDF Payloads

A critical challenge in generating a meaningful collision was crafting two valid PDF documents with identical SHA-1 digests that display completely different visual content. Researchers structured the PDF header and indirect object tables around identical collision blocks, ensuring that internal parser offsets would interpret the differing computational payloads into distinct visible rendered pages without invalidating document structure.

Fallout Across Developer Tools and Infrastructure

The public disclosure of the SHAttered collision revealed immediate security consequences across software ecosystems that still relied on SHA-1 integrity checks. Apache Subversion (SVN) repositories suffered immediate corruption when collision test files were committed, and critical developer toolchains experienced parsing panics. Bursztein explains how Google deployed counter-cryptanalysis filters in Gmail and Google Drive to detect shattered collision blocks before malicious files could be delivered, and emphasizes the urgent necessity of transitioning enterprise infrastructure to SHA-256 and SHA-3.

talks.title: DC to DEF CON Q&A
talks.teaser: Representatives Will Hurd and James Langevin discuss federal cybersecurity policymaking, legislative oversight, and government collaboration with the hacker community.
talks.summary:
Bridging Capitol Hill and the Hacker Community

Congressional Representatives Will Hurd and James Langevin participate in an interactive town hall session organized with the Atlantic Council Cyber Statecraft Initiative to bridge the divide between federal policymakers and technical security researchers. Both representatives bring specialized backgrounds to the discussion—Hurd as an undercover CIA operations officer and Langevin as co-founder of the Congressional Cybersecurity Caucus.

Legislative Challenges in Technical Policy

The discussion addresses the friction between statutory law and rapid technological evolution. The congressmen examine key statutory frameworks governing vulnerability research and reverse engineering, including the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act (CFAA) and the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA), exploring legislative efforts to establish safe harbor protections for good-faith security researchers.

Critical Infrastructure and Government Cyber Defense

Hurd and Langevin review federal incident response coordination, workforce shortages in public sector cybersecurity, and the vulnerability of legacy federal IT infrastructure. They analyze the impact of high-profile nation-state intrusions against government agencies and discuss the implementation of binding operational directives to phase out unmaintainable legacy protocols and insecure software vendors across federal civilian networks.

Interactive Community Dialogue

Audience members question the representatives on controversial policy topics, including government vulnerability hoarding, encryption backdoors, intelligence community surveillance authorities, and the risks of regulatory mandates stifle innovation. The congressmen emphasize that sustainable national cyber defense requires regular, transparent engagement between technical practitioners and legislative committees drafting national security policy.

talks.title: Offensive Malware Analysis: Dissecting OSX FruitFly
talks.teaser: Deconstructs the FruitFly macOS spyware variant by standing up a custom command-and-control server to stimulate and inspect binary capabilities.
talks.summary:
Discovery of the FruitFly Spyware

Patrick Wardle analyzes FruitFly, a stealthy macOS malware family that selectively compromised biomedical research institutions and academic targets while remaining undetected by commercial antivirus products for several years. The presentation focuses on the B variant of FruitFly, examining its custom evasion tradecraft and unique architectural components.

Deconstructing the Obfuscated Perl Dropper

The initial triage of the malware examines its primary dropper, which unusually relies on an obfuscated Perl script embedded within an application wrapper. Wardle breaks down the deobfuscation process, reconstructing the script's memory-resident staging routines, internal variable decoding, and execution flow that drops a native Mach-O binary payload onto the victim machine.

Standing Up a Custom Command and Control Server

Rather than undertaking months of tedious static binary disassembly, Wardle demonstrates an offensive malware analysis approach: standing up a custom command-and-control (C2) server to interact directly with infected hosts and stimulate latent capabilities. By observing protocol handshakes and reverse engineering network packet structures, researchers can command the live malware binary to trigger individual functionality in controlled sandbox environments.

Stimulating Hidden OS Level Capabilities

Using the custom C2 framework, Wardle maps out the extensive spying features of FruitFly, including remote screen capture, webcam activation, microphone recording, and synthetic mouse event injection using low-level CoreGraphics and I/O Kit APIs. To verify the malware's control over user interface events, Wardle details the creation of a custom mouse-sniffer tool that decodes synthetic event messages sent by the malware to the operating system, demonstrating how active protocol manipulation accelerates comprehensive reverse engineering.

talks.title: The Last CTF Talk You’ll Ever Need: AMA with 20 years of CTF Organizers
talks.teaser: Organizers from Legit BS, DDTEK, Kenshoto, and Ghetto Hackers review two decades of DEF CON Capture the Flag architecture, challenge design, and competition lore.
talks.summary:
Two Decades of DEF CON Capture the Flag

Capture the Flag (CTF) has served as the premier technical contest at DEF CON since its inception at DEF CON 4, evolving from rudimentary local network skirmishes into the most prestigious competitive hacking tournament in the world. A panel of past and present organizers representing Legit Business Syndicate, DDTEK, Kenshoto, Ghetto Hackers, and the Goon staff convene to chronicle twenty years of competition architecture, contest philosophy, and community culture.

Evolution of Challenge Design and Infrastructure

The organizers trace the technological trajectory of CTF games, from early physical server setups and unencrypted hub environments to complex virtualized networks, custom architecture hardware challenges, and high-throughput network scoring engines. They discuss the continuous game-theoretic struggle between organizers and competitors, detailing mechanisms developed to prevent teams from gaming scoreboard rules, sharing flags, or conducting out-of-bounds infrastructure denial of service.

The Crucible of Challenge Development

Panelists provide behind-the-scenes accounts of authoring zero-day style exploitation challenges, novel cryptographic puzzles, and esoteric binary reverse engineering problems under intense time constraints. They reflect on the balance between difficulty and playability, the impact of DARPA's Cyber Grand Challenge on automated vulnerability reasoning, and the logistical realities of maintaining uptime during seventy-two hours of adversarial traffic.

Competition Lore and the Black Badge Legacy

The session concludes with an open community AMA exploring legendary CTF incidents, concealed easter eggs, intense inter-team rivalries, and the enduring cultural significance of winning a DEF CON black badge. The organizers highlight how competitive CTF serves as a vital training ground for top-tier vulnerability researchers, shaping technical methodologies that define modern industry security practices.

talks.title: Trojan Tolerant Hardware & Supply Chain Security
talks.teaser: Proposes an architecture for building trusted, backdoor-tolerant hardware security modules out of untrusted commercial off-the-shelf components.
talks.summary:
Supply Chain Vulnerabilities in Silicon Fabrication

High-assurance security systems traditionally operate on the assumption that underlying hardware components are trustworthy. Vasilios Mavroudis and Dan Cvrcek challenge this foundational model, highlighting that modern integrated circuit fabrication is almost universally outsourced to overseas foundries where covert hardware Trojans or subtle manufacturing defects can be introduced without detection by standard post-fabrication tests.

Limitations of Hardware Verification

Traditional quality assurance and optical inspection techniques are incapable of reliably detecting stealthy hardware Trojans that activate only under rare clock conditions or subtle analogue environmental triggers. Because comprehensive destructive silicon forensics is economically infeasible for commercial deployments, organizations require an architectural approach to hardware trust that tolerates compromised components.

Architecting Backdoor Tolerant Security Modules

The authors introduce a high-assurance hardware architecture capable of surviving the compromise of individual integrated circuits. They present a proof-of-concept backdoor-tolerant Hardware Security Module (HSM) constructed entirely from low-cost, off-the-shelf commercial components. The design incorporates component diversification, threshold cryptography, and independent non-overlapping supply chains to ensure that no single vendor or foundry can unilaterally compromise system keys.

Enforcing Mutual Distrust Between Components

The core operational principle of the architecture is mutual distrust: critical cryptographic operations and random number generation are split across isolated heterogeneous microcontrollers that cross-verify outputs before signing or decrypting payloads. Benchmarks demonstrate that this multi-chip consensus model incurs minimal performance overhead while providing rigorous fault tolerance and confidentiality guarantees against malicious silicon modifications.

talks.title: MS Just Gave the Blue Team Tactical Nukes
talks.teaser: Evaluates Windows Defender ATP and Microsoft Advanced Threat Analytics detection mechanisms and presents tradecraft for red teams to evade behavioral telemetry.
talks.summary:
Enterprise Endpoint Telemetry Evolution

The introduction of Windows Defender Advanced Threat Protection (ATP) and Microsoft Advanced Threat Analytics (ATA) fundamentally altered enterprise defensive capabilities by moving beyond static signature detection toward pervasive endpoint behavioral telemetry and identity analytics within Windows 10 and Active Directory environments. Chris Thompson analyzes how these integrated defensive platforms impact traditional red team offensive tradecraft.

Behavioral Detections Across the Kill Chain

The presentation examines the specific heuristic models and kernel-level event tracing mechanisms deployed by Defender ATP to flag post-exploitation behavior. Thompson breaks down standard offensive workflows—including LSASS memory dumping, token manipulation, process injection, and WMI-based persistence—demonstrating how automated behavioral classifiers correlate anomalous API calls to trigger high-severity alerts in corporate security operations centers.

Evasion Strategies for Modern Defenses

To maintain stealth in hardened enterprise networks, red teams must adapt their tradecraft to circumvent behavioral monitoring. Thompson explores practical techniques for avoiding detection, including bypassing AMSI (Antimalware Scan Interface), modifying API calling sequences to blend with legitimate administrative tooling, manipulating parent-child process relationships, and conducting in-memory execution without touching disk or generating standard Sysmon event logs.

Operational Guidance for Attackers and Defenders

Thompson concludes with tactical recommendations for security practitioners operating in mature enterprise environments with centralized Event Log Forwarding. He details methods for executing stealthy Active Directory reconnaissance and lateral movement without generating anomalous Kerberos ticket requests or alerting identity behavior sensors, while emphasizing how defensive teams can fine-tune correlation rules to detect sophisticated evasion attempts.

talks.title: Weaponizing Machine Learning: Humanity Was Overrated
talks.teaser: Introduces DeepHack, an open-source neural network agent that uses reinforcement learning to autonomously discover and exploit vulnerabilities in web applications.
talks.summary:
Autonomous Vulnerability Discovery and Exploitation
